note: Metrics: pooled model, grid 32, raw uncapped E_bin. ROUGHNESS uses three normalisations: roughness_sd_norm / lap_sd_norm divide mean|dE| and Laplacian RMS by the P-mass-weighted SD of E_bin (OUTLIER-ROBUST, primary); roughness_iqr_norm divides by the mass-weighted 5-95 inter-percentile range; roughness_range_norm divides by the raw range (outlier-SENSITIVE, kept for reference). roughness_core_sd_norm is the SD-normalised |dE| restricted to the top-90% P-mass cells (common-support). r2 = P-weighted ANOVA R2 of E(s) given cell; wells_1_2_3 = persistent wells at 1/2/3 bits; spurious = fraction backed by <=8 strings; continuity = mass-weighted fraction of substitution neighbours in same/adjacent cell; occ_cv = CV of |bin|; occupied = occupied-cell fraction; eff_cells = exp(entropy of cell mass); components = 4-/8-connected occupied components (no basis is fully connected at G=32 except coupling_spectral on pooled/twitter); var_ratio = P-weighted axis-variance ratio (collapse guard); stability_deg = angle to the basis fit one year earlier.

pca.label: PCA (default)
pca.summary: Top-2 principal axes of the P-weighted indicator covariance.
pca.html:
Each string is its one-hot vector \(\mathbf{x}(s)\in\{0,1\}^{104}\); the basis is the top-2 eigenvectors of \(C=\mathbb{E}_P[(\mathbf{x}-\mu)(\mathbf{x}-\mu)^\top]\), computed exactly from the model marginals. By Eckart & Young (1936) this is the unique 2-D linear subspace maximising the captured variance (17–20%).

Why the default. On the pooled model PCA has the highest substitution continuity (0.375), is time-stable (9.8°, more stable than raw TICA/LDA), and is the smoothest on the robust full-surface metric (SD-normalised \(|\Delta E|=0.656\)); these orderings are not uniform across the four models (e.g. on bluesky2024 tempered_pca has higher continuity, 0.231 vs 0.171, and other bases are smoother on austen/twitter/bluesky).

Why the surface looks jagged. The within-cell energy spread (6.8 bits) makes \(E_{\mathrm{bin}}\) a noisy average, and 19% of the \(\ge 1\)-bit wells are "spurious" (backed by \(\le 8\) strings). This is a lattice/energy-summary artifact, not a real energy feature.

Eckart & Young, Psychometrika 1, 211–218 (1936), doi:10.1007/BF02288367.

coupling_spectral.label: Coupling spectral (Hopfield)
coupling_spectral.summary: Top-2 eigenvectors of the gauge-fixed coupling matrix J — directions of largest quadratic energy variation.
coupling_spectral.html:
For the pairwise model \(E(s)=-\tfrac12\mathbf{x}^\top\hat J\mathbf{x}\) (zero fields after double-centring each \(26\times26\) block). The basis is the top-2 eigenvectors of \(\hat J\): the Hopfield memory patterns (Hopfield 1982) along which the wells are oriented. It is genuinely distinct from PCA (principal angle > 20°).

Corrected smoothness claim (after outlier-robust normalisation). Its raw-range-normalised roughness is the lowest (0.055), but that is an artifact: its E_bin range (37 bits) is stretched by a few sparse cells, while its mass-weighted SD is small. On the outlier-robust SD-normalised metric it is the roughest (0.724, vs PCA's 0.656) and on the common-support core (top-90% mass cells) also the roughest (0.429 vs energy_aligned's 0.236). It does, however, give the most uniform occupancy on three of four models (CV 1.45 pooled, 1.27 twitter, 1.15 bluesky; energy_aligned is more uniform on Austen, 1.27 vs 1.47) and the fewest spurious wells (5%).

Assumptions / limitations. Forbidden pairs (\(V=-\infty\)) are set to zero coupling here. Substitution continuity is the lowest (0.083): \(x^\top\hat Jx\) is a non-local summary.

When it helps / misleads. Use it to see the well/attractor geometry and the uniform coverage. Do not read its smooth appearance as energy smoothness.

Hopfield, PNAS 79(8), 2554–2558 (1982), doi:10.1073/pnas.79.8.2554.

energy_aligned.label: Energy-aligned (PLS)
energy_aligned.summary: P-weighted regression of E(s) on the indicators; axis 2 is the deflated residual.
energy_aligned.html:
Axis 1 maximises \(\mathrm{Cov}_P[\mathbf{v}^\top\mathbf{x},\,E(s)]\), the P-weighted least-squares linear predictor of energy; axis 2 is the next (deflated) partial-least-squares component. Genuinely distinct from PCA (principal angle > 10°).

Optimality (verified in tests). The PLS loading is proportional to \(\mathrm{Cov}_P[\mathbf{x},E]\), so it achieves the maximum \(|\)covariance with energy\(|\) among unit directions.

What it buys. Cells are among the most energy-homogeneous (ANOVA \(R^2=0.69\)–0.80; coupling_spectral is higher on twitter/bluesky/pooled, tempered on Austen), so \(E_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is a faithful summary; and it is the smoothest on the common-support core (top-90% mass cells): core SD-normalised \(|\Delta E|=0.236\), the best of the five.

The tension (explicit). \(x=E\) smooths any surface only by collapsing equal-energy strings, destroying identity: substitution continuity is the lowest (0.145). Always read it alongside a neighbour-preservation metric.

When it helps / misleads. Use it to see energy-driven roughness and the well-amplitude ordering. Do not read it as a 2-D map of word identity.

tempered_pca.label: Tempered PCA
tempered_pca.summary: PCA of the covariance weighted by P^alpha (alpha=0.75 default).
tempered_pca.html:
The covariance is \(\sum_s P(s)^\alpha(\mathbf{x}(s)-m)(\mathbf{x}(s)-m)^\top\) (normalised): \(\alpha=1\) is PCA, \(\alpha=0\) is classical MDS. Down-weighting the common words spreads the rare ones into the plane.

Alpha choice — honest caveat. \(\alpha=0.75\) was selected on the same evaluation metrics used to compare the bases (not held-out). The scan (pooled, grid 32; SD-normalised \(|\Delta E|\)) is:

α\|ΔE\|/sdoccupiedcontinuity
0.251.2500.2060.432
0.500.9130.2950.401
0.750.6630.5160.319

No \(\alpha\) in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} gives a single connected component (4-/8-connected components at G=32: 0.25 \(\to\) 3/3, 0.5 \(\to\) 3/3, 0.75 \(\to\) 5/2), so the earlier "connected support" part of the criterion is unsatisfiable and is dropped; \(\alpha=0.75\) is kept on the smoother-surface criterion alone.

Limitations. Not energy-aligned (within-cell \(R^2=0.67\)); the down-weighting is a deliberate loss of mass-fidelity.

When it helps / misleads. Use it to equalise common vs rare words and inspect global geometry. Do not trust its energy levels.

lda.label: Well-discriminant (LDA)
lda.summary: Fisher discriminant axes of the string-level descent basins (best separates the wells).
lda.html:
The basis solves Fisher's criterion \(S_B\,v=\lambda C\,v\), with \(S_B=\sum_k\pi_k(\mu_k-\mu)(\mu_k-\mu)^\top\) the P-weighted between-basin scatter over the string-level descent basins. \(\lambda\) is the correlation ratio \(\eta^2\in[0,1]\); the top-2 axes best separate the landscape's wells (regularised to the 95%-variance subspace). Genuinely distinct from PCA (principal angle 8–17°).

Optimality (verified in tests). \(\lambda\) equals the correlation ratio, and a random direction's \(\eta^2\) never exceeds the top eigenvalue.

What it buys. Places strings by which well they belong to (substitution continuity 0.341, near PCA's 0.375), non-degenerate on all four models (coverage \(\ge 50\%\) of PCA, axis-variance ratio \(\le 1.7\)).

Limitations (honest). Least time-stable (23.0°, basin relabeling). It is not a locality-preserving projection: the LPP idea it replaces was audited and found vacuous (flat Laplacian spectrum on the full Hamming graph) or degenerate (flux-weighted, sparse models).

When it helps / misleads. Use it to see the wells as discriminable clusters. Do not use it across trajectory frames.

energy_metric.label: Energy-metric layout — DEGENERATE (diagnostic)
energy_metric.summary: Landmark-MDS (Isomap) of the substitution graph weighted by energy slope; found degenerate (y ~ energy ramp, x ~ linear). Diagnostic only.
energy_metric.html:
VERDICT: DEGENERATE — this is a diagnostic, not a recommended basis. The layout reproduces the degenerate λ→0 control (the energy ramp) mixed with a linear projection. On the pooled model the y-axis is 95% the energy ramp (R²(y,E)=0.948, Spearman 0.976), the x-axis is 98% linear in the one-hot indicators (linear R²=0.98), Kruskal stress is 0.88–0.92, and Austen occupancy is 0.18 (< half of PCA's 0.37).

Why. H(4,26) has diameter 4: 85.5% of string pairs are at Hamming distance 4 and the geodesic D-spread has CV 0.10 (near-equidistant), so MDS of the energy-weighted geodesic metric returns a near-Euclidean (linear) ball plus the energy ramp. The λ-sweep is degenerate end to end: R²(y,E) = 0.999 / 0.948 / 0.001 at λ×{0.25, 1, 4} of the flux-median scale — no intermediate λ escapes. The energy-weighted Laplacian-eigenmap comparator (w = exp(-ΔE²/ℓ²)) fails the same way or worse: coverage 0.076–0.089 (localised rare-direction with eigengap ≈ 3–6×10⁴) at finite ℓ, and a flat level-1 spectrum (eigengap 0) at ℓ→∞.

Why GP/BO and splines do not escape. GP/Bayesian optimisation has 2N = 913 952 free coordinates with a cheap differentiable objective and a trivial optimum without a constraint — the wrong tool for a low-dimensional black box. A spline layout x(u), y(u) with a feature vector u is again a parametric projection of word data, and with u = energy rank it is the degenerate control. Neither supplies a non-trivial organising principle.

Controls (also reported). `basis.energy_rank_layout` (λ→0: a boustrophedon raster sorted by energy, the quantile function of E — smooth at every scale, x,y encode only the density of states) and `basis.hamming_layout` (λ→∞: MDS of the pure Hamming geodesic, the near-equidistant graph geometry). Both are kept as the honest demonstration of the two limits, not as selectable bases.

Tenenbaum, de Silva & Langford, Science 290, 2319–2323 (2000), doi:10.1126/science.290.5500.2319. de Silva & Tenenbaum, Sparse multidimensional scaling using landmark points, Stanford Tech. Rep. (2004). Ceriotti, Tribello & Parrinello, PNAS 108(32), 13023–13028 (2011), doi:10.1073/pnas.1108486108. Becker & Karplus, J. Chem. Phys. 106, 1495 (1997).
